collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Raiders set the storehouse roof on fire: save the stores, or save the huts beside it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The raiders are gone, but they left fire behind: burning arrows in the thatch of the storehouse, and the flames are spreading to the huts beside it. (subject) wants to throw everyone at the storehouse, where the food for the dry season is. (friend) says the huts first, because people live there. There are not enough hands for both. What should they do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village forms a water line to the storehouse and saves most of the food. Two huts burn to the ground. Their families move in with neighbors. (subject) helps rebuild them, and does not sleep until they are done.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village saves the huts. The storehouse burns, and half the dry-season food with it. It will be a hungry season. (friend) says it was the right choice. (subject) agrees, and then goes and sits by the ashes for a long time.
